newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress welcomes offer to hold talks.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress welcomes offer to hold talks.

text.p: India's Congress party on Wednesday welcomed an offer by the ruling United Front coalition to hold talks to end a political impasse.

Congress general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad told reporters that the party president, Sitaram Kesri, had responded to a letter from the United Front offering to hold talks to resolve the political crisis.
"We welcome the formal discussion," Azad said, adding that Kesri had written back to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's alliance.
"The working committee has authorised the Congress president to take a decision with respect to finalising the names on behalf of the Congress party," Azad.

Earlier on Wednesday, the alliance named a three-member panel for the talks, comprised of Harkishan Singh Surjeet, general secretary of the Communist Party of India-Marxist, Jammu and Kashmir state Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah and Andhra Pradesh state Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu.
The two sides are seeking to mend fences before a vote of confidence in Deve Gowda's government set for Friday. It was not known when the talks would begin.
